ammonite-2020.gazette: Mary Anning pulled the first correctly identified ichthyosaur and the first complete plesiosaur out of the Lyme Regis cliffs and sold them to the men who wrote the papers. Her name stayed off most of those papers; the Geological Society of London, whose fellows bought and described her finds, would not elect a woman until the following century. The romance in the film is speculation. The ledger it sits on is not.

another-round-2020.gazette: Vinterberg signed the Dogme 95 manifesto in Copenhagen and shot its first film three years later, throwing out score, sets, and the tripod in exchange for a promise about what the image owed the world. Another Round keeps the inherited grammar — handheld, available light, scenes held long enough for actors to lose their footing — and points it at staff rooms and kitchen tables. The vow expired; the working method it produced is still the one on set.

boys-state-2020.gazette: The American Legion has run Boys State since 1935, handing a thousand or so teenagers an empty state government and a week to fill it. The 2018 Texas session convened in Austin, and the filmmakers covered it with documentary crews rather than reconstruction: the campaigns, the smears, and the vote counts are the ones that happened. What plays like a screenplay about American politics was gaveled into existence by seventeen-year-olds.
boys-state-2020.prism: The unsettling part isn't that the boys imitate adult politics badly. It's how fast the sharpest ones work out that the cynical move wins, and that nobody in Austin had to teach them.

da-5-bloods-2020.gazette: Lee cuts his fiction against the record — Hanoi Hannah's broadcasts, King's April 1967 break with the war, the arithmetic of Black soldiers dying at a rate far above their share of the country. The flashbacks arrive on grainy 16mm in a boxed-in frame, played by the same actors, unaged: the veterans remember themselves as they are now, while the archive keeps its own faces. The war footage was never set dressing here. It functions as a citation.

dick-johnson-is-dead-2020.gazette: Dick Johnson practiced psychiatry in Seattle until dementia forced him to close the office, and his daughter, a working cinematographer, began filming around the time he moved in with her. The deaths are staged — stunt doubles, rigged falls, a crew standing by — but the decline they rehearse against is on the calendar. Alzheimer's had already taken her mother, mostly unfilmed, which is the absence the whole project is built to avoid repeating.

mank-2020.gazette: In the autumn of 1934, MGM shot fake newsreels of drifters pledging their votes to Upton Sinclair and slotted them into California theaters between features; Sinclair lost the governorship that November. The film works outward from that campaign to the studio that ran it, to Hearst's table at San Simeon, and to the authorship fight over Citizen Kane that Pauline Kael reopened in 1971. Jack Fincher wrote the script in the 1990s. His son shot it decades later, black and white, in mono.
mank-2020.prism: The fake newsreels are the part that hasn't aged. A studio found out it could manufacture a public in a week, and the argument over whose name goes on Kane is a small quarrel happening inside a much larger discovery.

nomadland-2020.gazette: Empire, Nevada lost its gypsum plant in January 2011 and its ZIP code by that July, which is where the film opens and roughly where Jessica Bruder's reporting began. Linda May, Swankie, and Bob Wells appear as themselves; the Amazon CamperForce shifts and the Rubber Tramp Rendezvous outside Quartzsite are the actual programs, filmed where they run. Two professional actors move through a cast that had already lived the script.

one-night-in-miami-2020.gazette: The four men did spend the night of February 25, 1964 together at the Hampton House motel in Miami, hours after Cassius Clay took the heavyweight title off Sonny Liston. The dialogue is Kemp Powers's invention; the positions are documented — Malcolm X was weeks from breaking with the Nation of Islam, Sam Cooke had already recorded 'A Change Is Gonna Come' and was sitting on it. Within twelve months of that night, two of the four were dead.

sound-of-metal-2020.gazette: The mix moves between the room and the inside of Ruben's skull, built from binaural recording and a rendering of what a cochlear implant actually delivers: thin, metallic, fractionally out of step with the mouth producing it. Riz Ahmed trained on drums and in ASL for months and wore devices on set that masked his own hearing; Paul Raci grew up signing as the hearing son of Deaf parents, and the shelter residents are played by Deaf actors. It won the Academy Award for sound in 2021.
sound-of-metal-2020.prism: The implant sequence is the whole argument in one sound. It doesn't give the world back, it hands over a tinny copy — and Ruben only hears that copy after selling the trailer and the gear that would have let him stay somewhere people were already fluent.

the-disciple-2020.gazette: Hindustani khayal is measured in decades of riyaaz — practice before dawn, a single raga worked for years before anyone hears it — and Tamhane shoots that labour in long static takes that refuse to compress it. The ragas are real, the music direction came from practicing classical musicians, and the man playing Sharad trained as a vocalist before he acted. The tradition's own hard standard, that most disciples never arrive, is the plot.

the-woman-who-ran-2020.gazette: Hong hands out pages written that morning, shoots roughly in sequence with a crew small enough to fit inside a Seoul apartment, and lets an abrupt zoom do the work a cut would do elsewhere. Three visits, three conversations, mostly over coffee and grilled meat, with the men held at the edge of the frame or on the other side of a door. Berlin gave him the directing prize for it in 2020.

time-2020.gazette: Robert Richardson drew sixty years without parole for a 1997 bank robbery in Shreveport; his wife took a plea, served three and a half years, and started filming. Twenty years of her own home video — birthdays, sermons, the endless calls to a clerk's office — runs against footage Garrett Bradley shot herself, all of it graded to black and white. He came home in 2018.
time-2020.prism: Sixty years was his sentence. The film keeps counting what the household paid instead: six sons raised across visiting rooms, and a mother who spent two decades on hold. The tape exists at all because she assumed nobody else would bother keeping the record.

a-hero-2021.gazette: Farhadi builds on a practice that needs no invention: in Iran an unpaid private debt can hold a man in prison until his creditor is satisfied, and a two-day furlough is enough time to try something. He films it in Shiraz the way he filmed About Elly — long scenes, speech overlapping, no score arriving to mark who is lying. The camera stays at the height of an argument in a stairwell and lets the moral ground shift under it.

ahed-s-knee-2021.gazette: The title comes from a 2018 remark by an Israeli lawmaker that the teenage Palestinian protester Ahed Tamimi should have been shot in the knee. Lapid sets the film in an Arava desert village where a director screens his work under the culture ministry's library program and is asked to sign a form declaring which approved topics he will speak on — the same form Lapid was handed. The film is a restaging of the refusal he actually made.

c-mon-c-mon-2021.gazette: The interviews are genuine: in Detroit, New Orleans, New York and Los Angeles, Phoenix stayed in character with a recorder and asked real children what they expected the future to hold, and the answers went in unrewritten. Mills shot the whole picture in black and white so the documentary passages and the invented ones would sit in one register rather than announce themselves. No lines were handed to the kids.
c-mon-c-mon-2021.prism: The bet is that a scripted uncle and nephew can hold the screen next to children who aren't performing. Mostly they can — but Mills keeps giving the last word to someone who wandered in off a real street, which tells you where he thought the truth was sitting.
